To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the lysozymee gene is inactive in pluripotent chicken macrophage precursors and in myeloblastic cells, and there is no histone acetylaion of core histones in the vicinity of the lysozme gene; (2) in mature macrophage cells the lysozymmee gene is active and there is acetylation of H3 at its upstream silencer and of H4 and H3 at its enhancer element.

the lysozym gene is activated during chicken myelopoiesis in two distinct steps: (1) activation of the enhancer elements, which is linked to acetylation of H4, H3 and H2B at these elements; (2) activation of the gene, which is linked only to acetylation at H3.
acetylation of histone H3 is linked to the high-level expression of the lysozye gene during the development of macrophage cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the developmental activation of the lytic enzyme, lysozyme (Lys), in the chicken.
the role of histone acetylations in regulating gene expression during differentiation of the immune system.
the mechanisms that regulate the development and activation of the lyzoyme locus in chicken macrophages.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
acetylation at lysozyme enhancer elements is a prerequisite for lysozyme expression in chicken macrophages.

the developmental activation of Lys expression in chicken macrophages is linked to acetylation at cis-control elements but the acetylation of the Lys gene per se does not appear to be required for its activation.
H4 acetylated histones are required for developmental activation of the lyzoyme gene, but H3 acetylated histone are required for high-level Lys gene expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
acetylation of the core histones H4 and H3 is a key step in developmental activation and high-level stimulation of the chicken lysozyme (Lys) gene.

acetylation of H4 and H3 at the cis-control regions of the lyso gene is a key event during development and stimulation of macrophages, but that H3 acetylates at the lyso gene itself only during the high-level expression phase.
the lysozym gene is activated during chicken myeloid differentiation by a stepwise process in which H4 acetylations at the upstream enhancers are followed by H2B and finally H2A.Z acetylations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
core histone acetyl transferase activity is linked to developmental activation and high-level Lys gene expression.

core histone acetyltransferases and core histone deacetylases act in a coordinated fashion to regulate chromatin accessibility at the lysozmase locus during development and in response to stimulation with LPS.
the developmental and LPS-induced activation of the lyoysm gene in chicken macro-phages is linked to core H4 acetylati on at its cis-control elements.
